proposals.impact: reduce intro-to-q1 drop (2 of 3 sessions stalled at intro_load)
proposals.observation: In the 48-hour quiz window, 3 sessions loaded, 2 stalled at intro_load, 1 reached q1_shown, and 0 completed. That means the intro screen itself is the exit point for the majority of visitors. The copy or CTA on the quiz intro is not earning the click to question one.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro body copy and primary CTA button text. The current version almost certainly opens with a generic promise ("find out your money type" or similar) that 1,000 other coaches could have written. Replace it with a specific, grounded opening that names what Joel's ICP is actually feeling — earning well, building nothing, and not quite knowing why — then a CTA that names the action honestly rather than promising a result.
proposals.current_text: Find out your money type and start building a healthier relationship with money.
proposals.new_text:
You're earning more than you expected to at this age. You're also not building anything with it, and that gap has started to bother you.

This is a short set of questions about how you actually think and feel around money — not how you think you should. No right answers. Joel (MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner) uses your result to send you a short, honest piece on the specific pattern that tends to keep people in your position stuck.

Answer the questions honestly.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward Money Vigilance's 60% baseline
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has an open rate of 37.5% (6 opens from 16 sends), the lowest of the three active sequences. Money Vigilance sits at 60% and Money Avoidance at 50%. The gap is 22.5 percentage points between worst and best. Subject line is the most likely differentiator since list quality and send volume are comparable across all three.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email-1 in the Money Worship sequence. Money Worship as a pattern is characterised by the belief that more money will solve the underlying discomfort — a belief the ICP often holds without naming it. A subject line that names that specific tension (without hype or spiritual jargon) will earn the open in a way a generic prompt cannot.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Why money never feels like enough
proposals.new_text: Subject: You hit the number. It didn't fix it.

proposals.impact: restore failed workflow so competitive digest resumes publishing
proposals.observation: The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow failed at 10:16 UTC on 23 May (the only failed run among 22 total). This workflow presumably generates or publishes competitive or content-research digests that inform Joel's content queue. With 3 posts queued and 33 published, a steady queue depends on that pipeline staying healthy. A silent failure here means Joel may not notice until the queue runs dry.
proposals.proposal: Add a Slack or email failure notification step to the Funnel-Hack Digest workflow so that any future failure surfaces immediately rather than sitting silent in the GitHub Actions log. Also check the run log for the 23 May failure to identify the root cause — most likely a rate-limited API call or an expired token — and add a retry step with a 60-second back-off before the notification fires, so transient failures self-resolve without noise.
